item.title: Isomorphisms of $\ell^1$-crossed products of topological systems
item.description: arXiv:2610.33050v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We give a complete description of the isometric isomorphisms between the $\ell^1$-crossed products of actions of discrete groups on nonempty compact Hausdorff spaces. In particular, two such crossed products are isometrically isomorphic as Banach algebras if and only if the actions are topologically isomorphic. It follows that $\ell^1(G\curvearrowright X)$ remembers not just $X$ but even the acting group and the action, and is not determined by the transformation groupoid $G\ltimes X$ alone. The proof recovers $C(X)$ from the hermitian elements and uses the geometry of $L^p$-spaces to identify the invertible isometries. We also obtain analogous results for measurable actions.
item.dc:creator: Eusebio Gardella, Tabar\'e Roland

item.title: Weak type $(1,1)$ estimates for noncommutative maximal truncated rough singular integrals
item.description: arXiv:2610.33284v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove a weak type $(1,1)$ estimate for maximal truncations of noncommutative rough singular integrals whose angular kernels satisfy the classical $L\log L$ integrability and cancellation conditions. The main ingredient of the proof is a new linearization method for handling the maximal truncations acting on the bad functions arising from the noncommutative Calder\'on--Zygmund decomposition.
item.dc:creator: Junming Cao, Wei Li

item.title: On the transformation of unbounded convergent sequences by linear operators on Banach lattices
item.description: arXiv:2610.33289v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we introduce a weak variant of the concept of unbounded Dunford-Pettis linear operators, which we call unbounded weak Dunford-Pettis operators. We investigate the properties of this new class, establish inclusion and coincidence results involving unbounded Dunford-Pettis operators, and examine its relationship with the class of unbounded absolutely weakly continuous operators.
item.dc:creator: Fabr\'icio Santos, Ewerton Torres

item.title: Optimal Non-Homogeneous Improvements of the Anisotropic Hardy Inequality
item.description: arXiv:2610.33346v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider the Hardy inequality associated with a strongly convex Finsler norm $F$ on $\mathbb{R}^n$ and we study its optimal non-homogeneous improvements in the whole range $1<p<\infty$. We show that the anisotropic Hardy difference controls a weighted critical Sobolev norm when $1<p<n$, a weighted exponential integrability of Trudinger type when $p=n$, where the Hardy term is replaced by its Leray logarithmic correction, and a weighted H\"older seminorm when $p>n$, proving in each regime that the logarithmic weights appear with the optimal exponents. In the borderline case $p=n$ this extends to general functions the optimal exponent previously known only for anisotropically radial functions. The proofs rely on a common ground-state reduction, combined with a splitting into an $F_o$-radial and a mean-free part for $1<p\le n$, and with an anisotropic Morrey representation formula for $p>n$.
item.dc:creator: Giuseppina di Blasio, Giovanni Pisante, Georgios Psaradakis

item.title: Orthograph related to mutual (strong) numerical radius orthogonality on operator algebra
item.description: arXiv:2610.33422v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $\mathcal{B} (H)$ and $\mathcal{B} _s(H)$ be the algebra of all bounded linear operators on a complex Hilbert space $H$ and the Jordan algebra of all self-adjoint operators in $\mathcal{B} (H)$, respectively. In this paper, the orthographs by (strong) numerical radius orthogonality relation on $\mathcal{B} (H)$ or $\mathcal{B} _s(H)$ is introduced, and then the graph-theoretic properties of these orthographs, such as isolated vertices, connected components and the diameters, are discussed.
item.dc:creator: Shaoxing Sun, Jinchuan Hou, Xiaofei Qi

item.title: Noncommutative algebraic sets are not generically nc manifolds
item.description: arXiv:2610.33425v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A consequence of implicit function theorem is that any algebraic set is a complex manifold except at some singular points which form a strictly lower dimension algebraic subset. Accordingly, an non commutative implicit function theorem of Agler-McCarthy might suggest that a nc algebraic set is generically an nc manifold. However, in this paper, a type of nc polynomials is shown, whose zero locus has larger dimension than the nc manifold given by implicit function theorem.
item.dc:creator: Jiachen Lu

item.title: Quantum harmonic analysis and the Differential operators on weighted Bergman spaces of bounded symmetric domains
item.description:
arXiv:2610.33428v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We develop quantum harmonic analysis (QHA) for operators on the parametrized Bergman space $\mathcal{A}^2_
u(\Omega)$ of a bounded symmetric domain $\Omega$, extending the theory previously known for the unit ball. Building on this framework, we introduce a class of differential operators acting on operators on $\mathcal{A}^2_
u(\Omega)$. Combining these tools, we advance the theory of Toeplitz operators on $\mathcal{A}^2_
u(\Omega)$: we establish Toeplitz approximation results via the $\alpha$-Berezin transform, construct a differential operator $D_\alpha$ that shifts the $\alpha$-Berezin transform, and obtain several characterizations of the radial Toeplitz algebra -- including one via the uniformly continuous radial operators, and one via the domain of $D_\alpha$.
item.dc:creator: Matthew Dawson, Vishwa Dewage, Gestur Olafsson

item.title: Coordinate systems and maximal order complexity in Banach lattices
item.description: arXiv:2610.33462v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We resolve three questions arising from the study of coordinate systems and order convergence in Banach lattices. Firstly, every order (respectively, $\sigma$-order) basis $(e_n)$ for a Banach lattice $X=[e_n]$ is automatically a Schauder basis. In fact, the associated partial sum projections satisfy a maximal inequality, and hence every such basis is uniform. Secondly, we show that there is a separable Banach lattice $X$ in which the set $$ X_{\downarrow0}=\{(x_n)\in X^{\mathbb N}:x_1\geqslant x_2\geqslant\ldots\geqslant 0=\inf_nx_n\} $$ is $\mathbf{\Pi}^1_1$-complete. Finally, we construct a separable Banach lattice $Y$ for which the set $Y^{\uparrow\infty}$ of increasing positive sequences which are not order bounded is $\mathbf{\Pi}^1_1$-complete. It follows that neither $X_{\downarrow0}$ nor $Y^{\uparrow\infty}$ can be described in any simpler way than by the nonexistence of positive lower and upper bounds, respectively.
item.dc:creator: A. Avil\'es, C. Rosendal, M. A. Taylor, P. Tradacete

item.title: Ordinary algebras of complex-valued functions
item.description: arXiv:2610.33579v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A classical theorem due to Gleason, Kahane, and Zelazko states that every complex unital Banach algebra is ordinary, meaning that any linear functional mapping elements into their spectrum is a character. While Roitman and Sternfeld extended this property to algebras with bounded spectra-showing in particular that the algebra C(X) of continuous functions is ordinary when X is pseudocompact-the general case of C(X) for arbitrary topological spaces X appears to be open, as we could not locate any reference in this direction. In this paper, we show that the pseudocompactness condition is unnecessary, that is, C(X) is ordinary for every topological space X. This fact is obtained as a consequence of a more general result characterizing positive characters on a purely algebraic generalization of unital C*-algebras, which we introduce under the name of AC*-algebras. As applications, we obtain two necessary and sufficient conditions for a Tychonoff space X to be realcompact in terms of 1-evaluating linear functionals on C(X) and their continuity with respect to the compact-open topology. Finally, we establish a Banach--Stone type theorem showing that two realcompact spaces X and Y are homeomorphic if and only if C(X) and C(Y) are linearly isomorphic via a map that preserves invertibility.
item.dc:creator: Karim Boulabiar

item.title: Mixed-norm Herz-type Triebel-Lizorkin spaces
item.description: arXiv:2610.33618v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Based on mixed-norm Herz spaces, we introduce a new class of mixed-norm Herz-type Triebel-Lizorkin spaces. We establish their $\varphi$-transform characterization in the sense of Frazier and Jawerth and prove Sobolev embedding theorems for these spaces. The resulting embedding theorems extend and improve several known results for mixed-norm Triebel-Lizorkin spaces.
item.dc:creator: Douadi Drihem

item.title: Compactness of composition operators on Hardy spaces of homogeneous rooted trees
item.description: arXiv:2610.33717v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we present a complete characterization of the compactness of arbitrary finite linear combinations of composition operators acting on Hardy spaces of homogeneous rooted trees. In particular, we obtain a characterization of compactness for linear combinations satisfying the CNC. As an application, we give an affirmative answer to a conjecture raised by Choe et al. [Trans. Amer. Math. Soc. Ser. B 9(2022), 733--756] concerning such Hardy spaces. Furthermore, we establish the phenomenon of (double) difference cancellation for linear combinations of composition operators by constructing explicit examples.
item.dc:creator: Lei Liu, Wanxin Ma

item.title: On the power of adaption and randomization 2: Non-symmetric convex sets
item.description: arXiv:2610.33733v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $S:X\to Y$ be a bounded linear operator between real Banach spaces, and let $F\subset X$ be nonempty, bounded and convex. We prove $$a_{2n-1}(S,F)\le 27n\min \{ e^{\rm ran}_n (S,F), e^{\rm ada}_n (S,F)\}.$$ Here $a_k$ is the minimal worst-case error of continuous affine algorithms of rank at most $k$, and $e_n^{\rm ran}$ and $e_n^{\rm ada}$ are the minimal errors of adaptive randomized and deterministic algorithms using at most $n$ continuous linear measurements. This shows that the gain of adaption and randomization, and even nonlinearity, is limited by a factor $27n$ for approximation in convex sets. We discuss the optimality of the result by examples.
item.dc:creator: David Krieg, Erich Novak, Mario Ullrich

item.title: The Geometry of Limits in ReLU Function Spaces
item.description: arXiv:2610.33779v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the geometry and closure of spaces of functions realized by ReLU neural networks of fixed architecture. We first establish a general result about limits of continuous piecewise-linear (CPWL) functions: the minimum number of convex sets on which a function is affine is lower semicontinuous under pointwise convergence. The proof uses a connection to hypergraph coloring and a compactness principle, and yields quantitative bounds on the polyhedral complexity of continuous limits. We then characterize the functions realizable by shallow ReLU networks with vector-valued outputs, extending a known scalar-valued characterization. Using this and the geometry of limiting hyperplane arrangements, we prove that fixed-width shallow scalar ReLU realization spaces are closed in the weighted supremum norm on the whole input space. In contrast, we construct an explicit sequence of networks with architecture $(2,3,2\mid1)$ whose limit is not realizable by that architecture. Non-closedness holds both globally in weighted supremum norm and under uniform convergence on compact sets with nonempty interior, disproving a conjecture of Petersen, Raslan, and Voigtlaender. Finally, we show that non-closedness for a fixed scalar-output ReLU architecture necessarily involves a \emph{blow-up residue}, in which diverging output coefficients amplify an emerging linear dependence among hidden features. Together, these results provide geometric and functional-analytic tools for studying the boundaries and degenerations of ReLU realization spaces.
item.dc:creator: Kathryn A. Lindsey

item.title: A Borsuk-Ulam theorem for adaptive continuous measurements
item.description: arXiv:2610.33781v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove a Borsuk-Ulam theorem for adaptive measurements: if $2^n\le m$, then any $n$ adaptively chosen continuous functionals take identical values at two antipodal points of any sphere in $\mathbb{R}^m$. Consequently, at least $\lceil\log_2(m+1)\rceil$ adaptive continuous measurements are needed to learn the vectors of a ball in $\mathbb{R}^m$ with an error smaller than its radius, which matches the recently obtained upper bound up to one measurement. The bound extends to Bernstein widths in Banach spaces. The main idea of the proof was found by Claude Fable 5, an AI model developed by Anthropic, and we document the development in a last section.
item.dc:creator: Mario Ullrich

item.title: Banach-Cesaro positive operator-valued measure
item.description: arXiv:2610.33821v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We construct a family of bounded, finitely additive, covariant positive operator-valued measures (POVMs) on the real line by applying generalised Banach-Cesaro asymptotic averaging to locally finite covariant POVMs. In contrast to the strictly shift-invariant case, where countably additive operator measures are restricted to scalar multiples of a single fixed operator, the introduced covariant setting allows for non-commuting averaged operator values while successfully normalising the total mass. We develop an integration theory for complex-valued functions by taking the completion of simple integrable functions with respect to the continuous operator norm induced by the positive integral of their absolute values. The integration spaces for the original and the averaged measures are shown to possess distinct null classes. Finally, we introduce the operator-valued Fourier transform on these integration spaces and analyze the core algebraic constraints imposed by the covariance property on the exponential multipliers.
item.dc:creator: Sviatoslav V. Dzhenzher

item.title: Spectrality of convolution and product measures: a block decomposition approach
item.description:
arXiv:2610.33987v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the spectrality of convolution and product measures. Let~$\mu$~be a compactly supported Borel probability measure on~$\Bbb{R}^d$~such that ~$\mathcal{Z}(\widehat\mu)\cup\{0\}=T$~is an additive subgroup, and let~$
u$~be a Borel probability measure on~$\Bbb{R}^d$. We prove that~$\mu*
u$~is spectral if and only if~$T$~is a spectrum of~$\mu$, ~$
u$~is spectral, and~$supp
u$~is contained in a translate of the annihilator of~$T$. Moreover, every spectrum of~$\mu*
u$~decomposes into full cosets of~$T$, and every choice of one point from each coset is a spectrum of~$
u$. We also obtain a convolution-factor criterion which strengthens a result of Wu. As applications, we characterize the spectrality of~$L_{[0,1]}*
u$~and prove that the spectrality of~$L_{[0,1]^d}*
u$~implies that of~$
u$~without a compact support assumption. For product measures, we give necessary and sufficient conditions for an orthogonal set to be a spectrum by relating its block structure to spectra of the factors. No compact support assumptions are required.
item.dc:creator: Ting Zhou

item.title: Maximal Spaceability of the set of non-absolutely summing operators in quasi-Banach spaces
item.description: arXiv:2610.33999v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For every $0<p<1$, we establish maximal spaceability of the bounded operators on $\ell_p$ which fail to be $(r,s)$-absolutely summing for all $1\le s\le r<\infty$, using the coordinate-disjointization construction and Maddox's theorem. We give detailed isometric estimates and prove a corresponding maximal spaceability theorem inside the compact operators. The compact result is based on an explicit diagonal multiplier and a single weakly $1$-summable sequence witnessing the simultaneous failure of all admissible absolute summability conditions. A diagonal characterization, a logarithmic compact example, and extensions to operators with values in quasi-Banach spaces containing a copy of $\ell_p$ are also obtained. The constructed subspaces are isomorphic to $\ell_p$ and have maximal algebraic dimension whenever the ambient operator spaces have dimension $\mathfrak c$.
item.dc:creator: Daniel Ara\'ujo

item.title: Hyponormal and subnormal dual Toeplitz operators
item.description: arXiv:2610.34017v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we completely characterize hyponormal dual Toeplitz operators with general bounded measurable symbols by using the Douglas theorem in [R. G. Douglas, Proc. Amer. Math. Soc. 17 (1966), 413-415]. As an application, the hyponormality of dual Toeplitz operators with radial symbols and polynomial symbols in $z$ and $\bar{z}$ is characterized concretely. Moreover, we obtain complete characterizations for both subnormal dual Toeplitz operators with harmonic polynomial symbols and $\varTheta$-class dual Toeplitz operators with bounded harmonic symbols.
item.dc:creator: Linghui Kong, Yongning Li, Da Sun, Dechao Zheng

item.title: Noncommutative Mean Value Theorems for Free Noncommutative Functions
item.description: arXiv:2610.34032v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we study noncommutative analogues of the classical Cauchy and Lagrange mean value theorems in the setting of free noncommutative function theory. For noncommutative functions on a uniformly open noncommutative set, we prove a Cauchy-type mean value inequality involving the right noncommutative difference operator $\Delta_R$ and the G-derivative, and we establish a mean value theorem for noncommutative curves. Furthermore, we characterize uniform comparison (Lipschitz-type) inequalities at all matrix levels and prove a factorization theorem for noncommutative functions. The proofs combine the Hahn--Banach theorem, the fundamental theorem of calculus along a line segment, and the direct-sum compatibility of noncommutative functions.
item.dc:creator: Yali Du, Jun Jie Miao, Tianjiao Tan

item.title: Uniform Continuity of Boundary Crossing for Convex Sets
item.description: arXiv:2610.34039v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let C be an inhabited, bounded, open, convex subset of a Banach space, and phi the pointwise continuous mapping taking a pair of points, one inside C and one outside, to the point where the segment joining those points meets the boundary of C. We prove constructively that phi is uniformly continuous on the Cartesian product of a set well contained in C and the metric complement of C.
item.dc:creator: Douglas S. Bridges

item.title: The Strong Mankiewicz Property for Closed Convex Body in Normed Spaces
item.description: arXiv:2610.34113v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Mori and Ozawa raised a fundamental open question: whether every convex body in a normed space enjoys the strong Mankiewicz property (SMP). The SMP states that every surjective isometry from the convex body onto a convex subset of an arbitrary real normed space is necessarily real-affine, with no interior assumption imposed on the target convex set. In the present work, we settle this problem affirmatively.
item.dc:creator: Ruidong Wang, Jianglong Luo, Li Tang

item.title: Well located Banach spaces - A combined approach to L_1- preduals and Hilbert space
item.description: arXiv:2610.34152v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In the description of L_1- preduals on the one hand and of Hilbert spaces, on the other, one encounters the surprising appearance of similar classes of operators in terms of their extendibility properties in the setting of these two classes of spaces. It also turns out that the extension properties are closely tied to how the two classes of spaces are positioned inside the ambient spaces. It is well known that in the case of all subspaces being positioned inside a larger space Z as a complemented subspace leads to Z being (isomorphically) a Hilbert space whereas in the case of a Banach space X which is complemented inside all its superspaces, it turns out that X is an injective Banach space. In this paper, we shall be concerned mostly with such properties as demanding that X sit inside the ambient space as a locally complemented subspace (and sometimes as a Lipchitz retract). It turns out that the class of Banach spaces X determined by the indicated properties are precisely the class of L_1- preduals in the former case and of Hilbert spaces, in the latter. As an important consequence of this approach, we are led to several new characterisations of Hilbert spaces in terms of the extendibility of bounded linear maps coming from well-known operator (nonlinear operator) ideals.
item.dc:creator: M A Sofi

item.title: $(p,q)$-weighted dual curvature measures
item.description: arXiv:2610.34268v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study (p,q)-weighted dual curvature measures associated with a fixed nonnegative locally integrable Borel density satisfying a trace-regularity condition. These measures arise naturally from a variational formula for Wulff shapes. We establish the trace-regularity condition when g is pointwise \alpha-homogeneous for some \alpha\in R, or when g is radially non-increasing and continuous. For nontrivial even densities in either class, we prove existence results for the even version of the associated Minkowski problem under suitable assumptions. We also establish uniqueness when the prescribed measure has finite support, under a strict positivity assumption on the density and additional restrictions on the parameters. In the case of Lebesgue measure, our curvature measures reduce to those introduced by Lutwak, Yang, and Zhang, and our variational formulas recover their corresponding variational formula. For Gaussian measure, our results are related to those of Feng, Hu, and Xu, and Feng, Li, and Xu. Finally, we investigate the affine properties of the new measures and the associated mixed volumes.
item.dc:creator: Qingzhong Huang, Ai-Jun Li

item.title: Remarks on the Brascamp--Lieb inequality
item.description: arXiv:2610.34289v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove several variants of the Brascamp--Lieb inequality which are adapted to additional symmetries, weights, and non-Euclidean radial structures. First, an improved Brascamp--Lieb inequality for even functions yields a strengthened Pr\'ekopa--Leindler theorem for even strongly log-concave functions. We also record a Legendre-transform proof of a generalized log-Sobolev inequality for log-concave functions. Further results include a Brascamp--Lieb inequality with a concave weight, an unconditional second-order Poincar\'e inequality, a rotation-trick improvement for arbitrary even log-concave measures, and a Poincar\'e-type inequality associated with smooth norms.
item.dc:creator: Dario Cordero-Erausquin, Galyna V. Livshyts, Liran Rotem

item.title: On the isomorphism of the spaces $\mathcal{k}$ and $\mathcal{K}$
item.description: arXiv:2610.34421v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $1 \leqslant p \leqslant q < \infty$, let $\mathsf{X}$ be a separable $\mathcal{L}_p$-space and let $\mathsf{Y}$ be a separable $\mathcal{L}_q$-space. We show that the space $\mathfrak{L}(\mathsf{X},\mathsf{Y})$ of bounded linear operators from $\mathsf{X}$ into $\mathsf{Y}$ is isomorphic to $\mathfrak{L}(\ell_p,\ell_q)$ if, and only if, $\mathsf{Y}$ is complemented in its bidual. We also show that $\mathfrak{L}(\mathsf{Z},\ell_{\infty})$ is isomorphic to $\mathfrak{L}(c_0,\ell_{\infty})$ for every separable $\mathcal{L}_{\infty}$-space $\mathsf{Z}$. This extends and complements the earlier result of Arias and Farmer [On the structure of tensor products of $\ell_p$-spaces, Pacific J. Math.]. Based on this general result, we give a completely different proof of the main result of Astashkin, Le\'snik and Maligranda [Isomorphic structure of Ces\`aro and Tandori spaces, Canad. J. Math.], which states that the space $\mathcal{K}$ and its sequence counterpart $\mathcal{k}$ are isomorphic. Furthermore, we complete the picture by showing that the spaces $\mathcal{k}$ and $\mathcal{K}$, although isomorphic, are not isometric. Along the way, we show that for every infinite compact metrizable space $K$ the $\ell_{\infty}$-sum of copies of the space $\mathscr{M}(K)$ of regular Borel measures on $K$ is isomorphic to $( \bigoplus_{n=1}^{\infty} L_1[0,1])_{\ell_{\infty}} \approx \mathfrak{L}(\ell_1,L_1[0,1])$. This provides an abstract blueprint for another result of Astashkin, Le\'snik and Maligranda, namely that $\mathcal{K}$ is isomorphic to $( \bigoplus_{n=1}^{\infty} \mathscr{M}[0,1])_{\ell_{\infty}}$. Finally, we show that there are models of set theory without the Axiom of Choice in which the spaces $\mathcal{k}$ and $\mathcal{K}$ are no longer isomorphic. This last part was inspired by V\"ath's paper [The dual space of $L_{\infty}$ is $L_1$, Indag. Math. (N.S.)].
item.dc:creator: Tomasz Kiwerski, Jakub Tomaszewski

item.title: Isometric Theory for Greedy-Type Properties with Enlarged Greedy Sums
item.description: arXiv:2610.34686v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For a semi-normalized Markushevich basis, we study isometric almost-greedy inequalities in which a greedy sum of $\phi(m)$ terms is compared with coordinate projections onto at most $m$ terms. Here $\phi$ is any strictly increasing map of the nonnegative integers into themselves with $\phi(0)=0$. We sandwich $\phi$-almost greediness with constant $1$ ($\phi$-AG$_1$) between two levels of symmetry for largest coefficients (SLC): $$\phi\mbox{-SLC}_1\ \Longrightarrow\ \phi\mbox{-AG}_1\ \Longrightarrow\ \mbox{weak }\phi\mbox{-SLC}_1.$$ Both implications are equivalences if and only if $\phi(1)\le2$. We then characterize $\phi$-AG$_1$ by the weighted weak $\phi$-SLC or a single homogeneous norm inequality, called Property $(F_\phi)$.
item.dc:creator: Miguel Berasategui, Hung Viet Chu

item.title: $DW$-$L$-Weakly Compact Operators Between Banach Lattices
item.description: arXiv:2610.34981v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper we introduce a class of operators which we call $DW$-$L$-weakly compact operators. They carry disjointly weakly compact subsets of a Banach lattice onto $L$-weakly compact sets. The class of $DW$-$L$-weakly compact operators is closely related to two recently introduced classes of operators: almost $L$-weakly compact operators and order $L$-weakly compact operators. We show that $DW$-$L$-weakly compact operators are precisely those operators which are both almost $L$-weakly compact and order $L$-weakly compact. The adjoint and the order structure of $DW$-$L$-weakly compact operators are also considered.
item.dc:creator: Jin Xi Chen, Qiaozhi Wang

item.title: The Serre closure of Banach spaces
item.description: arXiv:2610.35259v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We determine the Serre closure of Banach spaces in the category of quasi-Banach spaces, that is, the smallest class of quasi-Banach spaces that contains all Banach spaces and is stable under subspaces, quotients, and extensions. Precisely, a quasi-Banach space $X$ belongs to this closure if and only if there exist constants $M$ and $k\in\mathbb N$ such that $$ \frac{\|x_1+\dots+x_n\|}{\|x_1\|+\dots+\|x_n\|}\leq M\log^k n $$ for every $n\geq 2$ and every $x_1,\dots,x_n\in X$; equivalently, $X$ is a quotient of an Orlicz sequence space $\ell(I,f_l)$, where $I$ is an index set and $f_l(t)$ is equivalent to $t\log^l(1/t)$ near zero. The proof combines geometrical estimates for quasi-Banach spaces and quasilinear maps with the study of higher order derived spaces associated to complex interpolation between $\ell_{2/3}$ and $\ell_2$. We provide examples of spaces in the Serre closure of Banach spaces that are not iterated extensions of Banach spaces and discuss some related problems.
item.dc:creator: F\'elix Cabello S\'anchez, Jes\'us M. F. Castillo, Ra\'ul Mart\'inez-Boh\'orquez, Jos\'e Navarro Garmendia

item.title: New thoughts on fractional Sobolev spaces
item.description: arXiv:2610.35279v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We introduce the concept of a fractional upper gradient and employ it to characterize the $p$-Muckenhoupt weighted $s$-fractional $p$-Sobolev spaces on $\mathbb R^d$ where $d\in\mathbb N$, $1<p<\infty$ and $0<s<1$.
item.dc:creator: Angha Agarwal, Pekka Koskela, Khanh Nguyen

item.title: Revisiting the Schwarz Lemma for the Pentablock: Counterexamples and Sharp Interpolation Criteria
item.description: arXiv:2610.35337v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Alshehri and Lykova (\emph{J. Geom. Anal.} \textbf{33} (2023)) formulated a Schwarz lemma for the pentablock $P$, giving a criterion for the existence of an analytic map from the unit disc $\mathbb D$ into the closed pentablock $\overline P$ that sends the origin to the origin and a prescribed point $\lambda_0\in\mathbb D$ to a given point $x_0\in\overline P$. We show that the sufficiency direction of their criterion is false. We identify the underlying error as the extension to the open unit disc of a Fej\'er--Riesz identity that is valid only on the unit circle. We establish a corrected necessary and sufficient interpolation criterion when the last two components are prescribed by a fixed rational $\Gamma$-inner function and resolve the special case $s_0=0$. Using the Poisson integral representation of the associated outer spectral factor, we obtain a sharp comparison between the corrected bound and the bound proposed by Alshehri and Lykova, with a precise characterization of equality. We further express the logarithmic difference between these bounds as a nonnegative Green potential, thereby quantifying the discrepancy in terms of the derivative of the first coordinate of the prescribed $\Gamma$-inner function. Finally, we formulate a variational problem over rational $\Gamma$-inner interpolants satisfying the prescribed two-point conditions. We show that the supremum of the associated outer-factor quantities determines the maximal admissible modulus of the first coordinate among pentablock-valued interpolants whose last two components belong to this class. Equivalently, this extremal problem reduces to minimizing the corresponding Green potential. We conclude by discussing the remaining problem of characterizing unrestricted Schwarz interpolation for the pentablock and its connection with the Lempert function.
item.dc:creator: Shubhankar Mandal, Avijit Pal, Bhaskar Paul

item.title: From one particle to N particles: uniform transport-information and log-Sobolev inequalities for Coulomb gases on the torus
item.description: arXiv:2610.35350v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study how a functional inequality satisfied by the one-particle conditional distributions of a Gibbs measure, with a constant independent of the positions of the other particles, can be propagated to the whole N -particle system, with a constant independent of N , when the interaction is singular. Our model is the Coulomb gas on the torus T 3 in the mean-field regime. We distinguish two mechanisms. The first one is a dependent tensorization, governed by Dobrushin-Wu interdependence coefficients. It yields uniform Poincar{\'e} and transport-information W 2 I inequalities with fully explicit constants. We explain why this mechanism does not extend to the log-Sobolev inequality: the Zegarlinski-type coefficients, which require pointwise bounds on the interaction, are infinite. The second mechanism is a tensorization with a defect. Using a uniform bound on the partition function due to Duerinckx and Jabin, it yields a uniform log-Sobolev inequality for the Coulomb gas on T 3 at small charge. We identify the assumptions on the interaction under which each mechanism applies. All the results are then extended to the two-dimensional Coulomb gas and to periodic Riesz gases 1/|x|^s , 0 < s $\le$ 1. The extension to d $\ge$ 4 is also discussed.
item.dc:creator: A Guillin (LMBP), W Liu (LMBP), B Nectoux (LMBP), L Wu (LMBP)

item.title: Converse symplectic interlacing via low-rank singular value perturbations
item.description: arXiv:2610.35376v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The symplectic interlacing theorem states that the symplectic spectrum of a $2n \times 2n$ real symmetric positive definite matrix satisfies a $2k$-step interlacing relation with the symplectic spectrum of every $2(n-k) \times 2(n-k)$ $s$-principal submatrix. We prove the converse in this paper. More precisely, given a positive global symplectic spectrum of size $n$ and a positive local symplectic spectrum of size $n-k$ satisfying the $2k$-step interlacing inequalities, we construct a $2n \times 2n$ real symmetric positive definite matrix having the prescribed global symplectic spectrum and a $2(n-k) \times 2(n-k)$ $s$-principal submatrix of it having the prescribed local symplectic spectrum. Our main tool is a reduction of $s$-principal compression to a rank-$k$ singular value perturbation. In the context of the Gaussian quantum marginal problem, our result implies that the symplectic interlacing inequalities are not merely necessary conditions on Gaussian marginals, but are also the complete spectral compatibility conditions for the global-versus-local-mode marginal problem.
item.dc:creator: Priyanka Grover, Hemant K. Mishra, Sarishti Singh, Temjensangba

item.title: Compact linear combination of composition operators on weighted Bergman-Orlicz spaces induced by doubling weights
item.description: arXiv:2610.35415v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $A^{\Psi}_{\omega}(\mathbb{D})$ be the weighted Bergman-Orlicz spaces induced by doubling weights $\omega$ on the unit disk $\mathbb D$. Suppose Orlicz function $\Psi$ satisfies the $\Delta_{2}$-condition. In this paper, the compactness of finite linear combination of composition operators on $A^{\Psi}_{\omega}(\mathbb{D})$ are completely characterized in terms of Julia-Carath\'eodory type conditions and vanishing Carleson measure, respectively.
item.dc:creator: Yucheng Li, Zhiyu Wang, Liankuo Zhao

item.title: Sharp Norm Approximation of Covering Markov Operators
item.description: arXiv:2610.35575v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the operator-norm approximation of Markov operators associated with finite graph coverings. Let $q:Y\to X$ be a connected covering of degree $d\geq 2$ between finite connected graphs, and let $A_q:C(Y)\to C(X)$ be its fiber-averaging operator. We show that $A_q$ is not a finite convex combination of extreme Markov operators, although such combinations approximate $A_q$ arbitrarily well in operator norm. We determine the exact distances from $A_q$ to convex combinations of at most $m$ extreme Markov operators, with arbitrary or equal convex weights. If $m=kd+r$, where $k\geq 0$ and $1\leq r\leq d$, these distances are $2(d-r+1)/[d(k(d-r+1)+1)]$ and $2r(d-r+1)/(dm)$, respectively. Both distances are attained and depend only on the covering degree $d$ and the number of terms $m$. We also determine when equal weights are optimal and quantify the additional approximation error when they are not. Our proofs use total-variation estimates and continuous rearrangements of labelled weighted atoms. In particular, the unrestricted errors have a common scaled limit, while the equal-weight errors exhibit residue-dependent asymptotic behavior.
item.dc:creator: H\"ulya Duru, Serkan \.Ilter, Ayg\"ul Bilgin

item.title: Boundedness and continuity of phase-corrected gradients on Sobolev spaces
item.description:
arXiv:2610.35584v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For a function $\psi: \mathbb{R}^d ightarrow \mathbb{C}$, we define the phase-corrected gradient $
abla_{\!\circ} \psi = |\psi|^{-1} \overline{\psi}\,
abla\psi$ and study the regularity of the map $\psi \mapsto 
abla_{\!\circ} \psi$ on Sobolev spaces. Since $\mathrm{Re}[
abla_{\!\circ} \psi] = 
abla |\psi|$, the phase-corrected gradient fits naturally into the framework of nonlinear composition operators. Its imaginary part $\Lambda = \mathrm{Im}[
abla_{\!\circ} \psi]$, on the other hand, plays a key role in quantum hydrodynamic models. We prove that $\psi \mapsto 
abla_{\!\circ} \psi$ is bounded and continuous from $W^{s,2}(\mathbb{R}^d)$ to $W^{s-1,2}(\mathbb{R}^d)$ for $1 \leq s <  rac32$, and we show that the threshold $s =  rac32$ is sharp. In particular, this answers an open question concerning the continuity of the map $\psi \mapsto |\psi|$ on Sobolev spaces. We also show that our results remain valid for functions that do not necessarily decay at infinity, a relevant setting in the context of Ginzburg--Landau theory. Finally, we extend our analysis to more general phase-corrected gradients of the form $f(|\psi|^{-1} \psi) 
abla \psi$, where $f: \mathbb{S}^1 ightarrow \mathbb{C}$ is Lipschitz, and discuss implications for certain parabolic PDEs.
item.dc:creator: Lars Eric Hientzsch, Raffaele Scandone, Robert Wegner

item.title: Characterizations of the unit vector basis of $c_0$ or $\ell_p$ among minimal systems
item.description: arXiv:2610.35726v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Given a minimal system E for a Banach space X, Casazza, Dilworth, Kutzarova and Motakis introduced a multiplication $\otimes$ on span(E) and studied the Schauder bases for which $\|x \otimes y\|\approx \|x\|\|y\|$ asking whether every such basis is equivalent to the canonical unit vector basis of $c_0$ or $\ell_p$. We continue this study in the more general setting of minimal systems that are not assumed to be Schauder bases, and we obtain positive answers under hypotheses that are formally weaker than the ones considered so far: partial democracy instead of democracy or bidemocracy, and truncation quasi-greediness instead of quasi-greediness. Along the way we show that the above multiplicative estimate forces invariance under translations, we characterize when such a minimal system is a Schauder basis, and we give examples showing that the one-sided variants of the estimate behave very differently.
item.dc:creator: Miguel Berasategui, Pablo M. Bern\'a, Stephen J. Dilworth, Denka Kutzarova, Timur Oikhberg

item.title: Variational relaxation and gradient flows for degenerate elliptic conductivity problems
item.description: arXiv:2610.33173v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We develop a convex-analytic $L^2$-framework for gradient flows of pumping-energy functionals coupled with elliptic state equations and an evolving nonnegative conductivity $a\geq 0$. The main difficulty is that the conductivity may be merely square-integrable, or degenerate, and formal differentiation need not produce an $L^2$-subgradient. After imposing the strictly positive lower cutoff $r+a\geq r>0$, we define the pumping-energy functional by a variational formula, prove convexity and lower semicontinuity, and show that its $L^2$-subdifferential is nonempty if and only if the pressure gradient belongs to $L^4$. We also obtain a unique maximal-monotone $L^2$-gradient flow satisfying an energy identity. Moreover, we prove Mosco convergence of the pumping-energy functionals as the cutoff vanishes. An inverse-moment conductivity constraint provides a weak alternative to a uniform positive lower bound. For nonlinear laws $a=\mu(b)$, primal and flux representations distinguish two complementary regimes. If $\mu$ is concave, the pumping-energy functional remains convex, and we characterize its $L^2$-subdifferential and the induced gradient flow. If $1/\mu$ is concave, the pumping-energy functional is concave, and therefore its negative is convex. We construct its pointwise gradient flow on a uniformly elliptic box. Admissible stationary points for power laws yield $p$-Laplacian equations with $p>2$ and $1 < p < 2$, respectively.
item.dc:creator: Jan Haskovec, Peter Markowich, Stefano Zampini

item.title: Mass concentration and ground states of Fermi systems in Hartree--Fock model with potentials
item.description: arXiv:2610.33530v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Understanding the onset and mechanism of collapse at critical attractive interaction is a fundamental problem in the variational theory of finite fermionic systems. In this paper, we study this problem within the Hartree--Fock framework under various trapping potentials. By establishing a finite-rank Hartree-type Gagliardo--Nirenberg--Sobolev inequality, we identify a critical threshold $\mathcal{K}^{(N)}$ governing the existence of ground states. We then determine the concentration behavior of ground states as the interaction parameter approaches $\mathcal{K}^{(N)}$. To reveal how the geometry of the trap influences this critical phenomenon, we consider three representative classes of potentials: polynomial-type potentials, ring-shaped potentials, and potentials whose zero set has nonempty interior. For each class, we derive the concentration scale and sharp asymptotics of the least energy. The resulting regimes are qualitatively different, showing that both the location and the rate of concentration are selected by the local geometry of the potential near its minimum set. In contrast to scalar Hartree problems, the nonlocal interaction is coupled here with pairwise $L^2$-orthogonality constraints, and their interplay creates substantial difficulties in the compactness and blow-up analysis.
item.dc:creator: Zhuocheng Li, Yuan-da Wu, Xiaoyu Zeng

item.title: The closed convex hull of all associative copulas is a Z-set in the family of all bivariate Schur concave copulas, and related results
item.description: arXiv:2610.33646v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Very recently, Problem 2.5 stated by Mesiar and Sarkoci in \cite{MeSa} and originally formulated by Durante was answered in the negative by \v{S}eliga \cite{Sel}. The author showed that the closed convex hull of all bivariate associative copulas is a proper subset of the family of all Schur concave copulas, and even computed the exact uniform distance of his counterexamples to the closed convex hull (so that the Hausdorff distance between the two families is at least $\frac32-\sqrt{2}$). Using the fact that every bivariate associative copula can be represented as a (finite or countably infinite) ordinal sum of Archimedean copulas and the minimum copula $M$, and working with the Markov kernels of Archimedean copulas, we first give an alternative, simple proof of the strict inclusion. We do so by showing that convex combinations of associative copulas can assign only very little mass to \new{staircase-shaped unions of small squares covering} certain line segments parallel to the main diagonal, a result we later extend to so-called chains and staircases. Building on the first observation, we then go one step further and show that, from a topological perspective, the closed convex hull of all associative copulas is a very small subset of the Schur concave family, namely a so-called $Z$-set, and that the family of associative copulas is, in turn, a $Z$-set in its closed convex hull.
item.dc:creator: Wolfgang Trutschnig, Manuel \'Ubeda-Flores

item.title: Dirichlet problem on locally finite graphs (revised and extended version)
item.description: arXiv:2610.33703v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study existence and uniqueness of solutions to the vertex-weighted Dirichlet problem on locally finite graphs. Let $B$ be a subset of the vertices of a connected graph $G$. The Dirichlet problem asks for a function whose discrete Laplacian is prescribed on $V\setminus B$ and whose values are prescribed on $B$. Each infinite connected component of $G\setminus B$ is called an end of $G$ relative to $B$. On finite graphs we show that the solution is the limit of an averaging process, with an explicit geometric rate given by the spectrum of the random walk, and is also the limit of the heat flow and the minimizer of an energy functional. On infinite graphs we prove two existence theorems: one with no assumption on vertex degrees, under a finite-width condition and summable data, and one for bounded data on graphs of bounded degree, where the solution is also unique among bounded functions. If there are no ends, the Dirichlet problem has exactly one solution. If there are $l$ ends, the solution set, when nonempty, has dimension at least $l$; each end carries a positive harmonic function vanishing on $B$. Calling an end parabolic when the random walk started in it hits $B$ almost surely, we show that this function can be taken bounded exactly on non-parabolic ends and is necessarily unbounded on parabolic ones, a discrete analogue of a theorem of Li and Tam. Consequently, bounded solutions are unique if and only if every end is parabolic.
item.arxiv:journal_reference: M. Javaheri, Dirichlet problem on locally finite graphs, Discrete Appl. Math. 155 (2007), no. 18, 2496--2506
item.dc:creator: Mohammad Javaheri

item.title: The $C_p$ conjecture of Muckenhoupt
item.description: arXiv:2610.34099v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We give an affirmative answer to Muckenhoupt's $C_p$ conjecture: for $1<p<\infty$, the $C_p$ condition is necessary and sufficient for the weighted $L^p(w)$ norm inequality relating the Hilbert transform and the Hardy--Littlewood maximal operator. We also show that the $C_p$ condition is necessary and sufficient for the weighted Fefferman--Stein inequality.
item.dc:creator: Andrei K. Lerner, Sheldy Ombrosi

item.title: Operator systems in \'etale groupoid C*-algebras
item.description: arXiv:2610.34269v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study operator systems arising from positivity domains of \'etale groupoids with compact unit space. Extending Kavruk's enough unitaries principle we show that such operator systems are hyperrigid in the C$^*$-algebra they generate. We focus on operator systems of positivity domains in UHF algebras and, by identifying them with Cantor graph operator systems, we show that they are hyperrigid. Furthermore, we show that in general, such a characterization is not possible when the \'etaleness condition of the underlying groupoid is removed, due to the failure of reduced spectral and compact operator synthesis.
item.dc:creator: Georgios Baziotis, Douglas Farenick, Evgenios T. A. Kakariadis, Malte Leimbach, Lyudmila Turowska, Walter D. van Suijlekom

item.title: Independent powers and bounded Fourier partial sums in $L^1$
item.description: arXiv:2610.34587v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We construct a probability measure on the circle with independent convolution powers and uniformly bounded symmetric Fourier partial sums in $L^1$. Every positive convolution power is therefore singular with respect to Haar measure. The measure is Rajchman. The construction answers a question of Andersson concerning measures with bounded Fourier partial sums outside the radical of $L^1$, and contrasts with his theorem that the classical examples of Weiss, Katznelson, and Brown-Hewitt have convolution squares in $L^2$. Our proof combines sparse probability blocks, an endpoint $L\log L$ estimate, and a diagonal generalized Riesz product. Exact factorization of local moments permits the simultaneous separation of all convolution powers by Brown's singularity criterion. By the classical spectral theory of independent-power measures, its spectrum is the closed unit disc. In particular, it has non-natural spectrum and induces a non-decomposable convolution operator on $L^1$. The image of the measure in $M(\mathbb T)/L^1(\mathbb T)$ has spectral radius one, and the closed unital algebra it generates in $M(\mathbb T)$ is isometrically isomorphic to $\ell^1(\mathbb N_0)$.
item.dc:creator: Przemys{\l}aw Ohrysko

item.title: Measure Convergence under Weak Domination for Unitarily Invariant Norms on Finite von Neumann Algebras
item.description: arXiv:2610.34776v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The classical Lebesgue dominated convergence theorem (DCT) is a cornerstone in commutative measure theory, while its extension to the noncommutative setting has remained a longstanding challenge due to the barriers posed by the noncommutative structure. Let \(\alpha\) be a unitarily invariant norm defined on a diffuse tracial von Neumann algebra \((\mathcal{M}, \tau)\), let $L^\alpha(\mathcal M, \tau)$ be the completion of $\mathcal M$ with respect to the norm $\alpha$(which includes all $L^p(\mathcal M, \tau)$ as special cases). In this paper, by replacing ``almost everywhere convergence" with Nelson's convergence in measure, we establish a noncommutative analog of the dominated convergence theorem for $L^\alpha(\mathcal M, \tau)$ under a { significantly weaker dominating condition} than those previously considered. For instance, in a \(II_1\) factor \(\mathcal{M}\), if \(P\) is a projection with \(\tau(P)=\frac{1}{n}\), then \(n^2 P\) ``dominates" every operator of norm \(\leq n\). As an application, we obtain a complete characterization of center-preserving $*$-automorphism of finite von Neumann algebras, which unifies and extends the earlier works of Kadison and Haagerup on the structure of automorphisms.
item.dc:creator: Yanni Chen, Don Hadwin, Junhao Shen, Ye Zhang

item.title: Comparisons of benchmark equivalence relations
item.description:
arXiv:2610.35025v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We determine the Borel-reducibility comparison of each pair of $\mathbf\Pi^0_3$ benchmark equivalence relations in Gao's monograph. The additional comparisons we prove are $E_\infty\leq_B c_0$, $E_\infty
leq_B\ell_p$ for $2<p<\infty$, $\ell_p
leq_B{\equiv_m}$ for $2<p<\infty$, $c_0
leq_B{\equiv_m}$, $c_0
leq_B\ell_\infty^+$ and $\equiv_m
leq_B\ell_\infty^+$. Together with the previous positive direction, these give $\ell_p\leq_B{\equiv_m}$ if and only if $p\leq2$. These answer several questions in Gao's monograph and Kanovei' monograph. We also prove that unitary equivalence of all bounded linear operators is not Borel reducible to $\equiv_m$. This answers a question of Ding and Gao. Equivalently, unitary equivalence of arbitrary representations of $F_\infty$ is strictly more complicated than that of arbitrary representations of $\mathbb Z$. This answers a question of Thomas.
item.dc:creator: Ruijun Wang

item.title: The norm reveals projections in the positive unit sphere of an arbitrary C*-algebra
item.description: arXiv:2610.35290v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We show how a simple metric condition in terms of the C$^*$-norm of an arbitrary C$^*$-algebra $A$ can be employed to determine those norm-one positive elements which are projections. Concretely, if we write $S_{A^+}$ for the intersection of the positive cone and the unit sphere of $A$, we establish that an element $a \in S_{A^+}$ is a projection if, and only if, $$\{a\} = \left\{x\in S_{A^+}: \|x-z\| = 1 \hbox{ for all } z\in S_{A^+}\hbox{ with } \|a-z\|=1 \right\}.$$ This proves a conjecture which has been previously confirmed for von Neumann algebras and unital C$^*$-algebras. In the setting of not necessarily unital JB$^*$-algebras, the Shirshov--Cohn theorem is invoked to obtain a similar metric characterisation of projections. In the wider setting of JB$^*$-triples, we show how a metric characterisation in terms of inner ideals can be established to determine non-zero tripotents.
item.dc:creator: Antonio M. Peralta, Pedro Saavedra

item.title: Multilinear extrapolation on Banach function spaces
item.description: arXiv:2610.35364v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We solve an open problem on the multilinear Rubio de Francia extrapolation on Banach function spaces. The first result states that, under the assumption of boundedness of the multisublinear Hardy-Littlewood maximal operator, the multivariable boundedness on Banach function spaces can be extrapolated from some weighted Lebesgue space, including the cases where some exponents may be infinite. Under the same assumption, the second result asserts that if a multilinear operator is bounded on some weighted Lebesgue space, then its compactness can be extrapolated from some unweighted Lebesgue space to Banach function spaces. Our results do not require any convexity or concavity conditions on Banach function spaces. The main ingredients in the proof are a multilinear version of the Rubio de Francia algorithm, a stopping-time argument, convex analysis, and a compactness criterion on Banach function spaces. As applications of extrapolation theorems, we obtain multilinear extrapolation for the boundedness and compactness of commutators on Banach function spaces. These results can be further applied to specific operators, which cover both the full range case including multilinear Calder\'{o}n-Zygmund operators, multilinear pseudo-differential operators, and bilinear paraproducts, and the limited range case including the bilinear Hilbert transform, multilinear rough singular integrals, and bilinear oscillatory Fourier multipliers.
item.dc:creator: Mingming Cao

item.title: Unique direct-sum decompositions of infinite-dimensional unitary representations of the infinite dihedral group via real CMV matrices
item.description: arXiv:2610.35371v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Unitary representations of the infinite dihedral group arise naturally and play an important role in a wide range of areas including mathematics, physics, and engineering. CMV matrices, introduced by Cantero, Moral, and Vel\'azquez, are five-diagonal unitary matrices that are standard tools in the theory of orthogonal polynomials on the unit circle. It is known that every unitary representation of the infinite dihedral group on a separable Hilbert space admits a discrete direct-sum decomposition into representations arising from the natural factorizations of real CMV matrices and copies of two exceptional one-dimensional irreducible representations. We prove that such a decomposition is unique up to unitary equivalence when the summands arising from real CMV matrices are grouped according to their multiplicities and the spectral measures of the corresponding matrices are mutually singular across distinct multiplicities. Furthermore, we show that the representation associated with each such real CMV matrix $C$ admits a direct integral decomposition into irreducible unitary representations with respect to the push-forward of the restriction of the spectral measure of $C$ to the closed upper half circle. These results make it possible to study the structure of unitary representations of the infinite dihedral group using CMV matrices and the theory of orthogonal polynomials on the unit circle.
item.dc:creator: Yuki Fujii

item.title: The divergence of continuously differentiable vector fields
item.description: arXiv:2610.35452v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: For $m\geq 2$, we give a complete characterisation of the continuous functions on $\mathbb{R}^m$ that are divergences of continuously differentiable vector fields. The characterisation is formulated in terms of distributions and, equivalently, in terms of the continuous dual of a suitably topologised subspace of the Arens--Eells space. The two implications yield contrasting applications. First, there exists a compactly supported continuous function which is the divergence of a bounded Lipschitz vector field but not of any continuously differentiable vector field. Second, every continuous function whose distributional partial derivatives are locally $m$-integrable (the critical exponent for Sobolev embedding) is the divergence of a continuously differentiable vector field.
item.dc:creator: Thierry De Pauw

item.title: Entropic hypocoercivity via the Polchinski flow: an application to the lattice sine-Gordon model
item.description: arXiv:2610.35759v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We develop a multiscale criterion for exponential decay of relative entropy in the canonical stochastic quantization of lattice field theories, the underdamped Langevin dynamics of the field and its momentum. For smooth bounded perturbations of Gaussian fields, the criterion requires the uniform operator-norm bound on the smoothed interaction Hessian along the Polchinski flow of Bauerschmidt and Bodineau to have a small $L^2$ norm in the scale variable. The decay constants depend only on this $L^2$ norm and the friction. The proof measures the transfer of momentum dissipation to position on the same scales that decompose entropy. A phase-space extension of the Polchinski flow gives Gaussian coarse-graining that commutes with free kinetic evolution. Integrating position--momentum cross terms over these scales yields a corrector bounded by entropy. A force defect accounts for changes in the averaged interaction force away from equilibrium; its evolution in scale controls the errors in the kinetic estimate. For the massive two-dimensional lattice sine--Gordon model with $0<\beta<4\pi$ and small dimensionless local coupling, the criterion gives entropy decay for all finite-entropy initial laws, uniformly in the lattice spacing and the volume. For friction proportional to the mass $m$, the rate has optimal order $m$.
item.dc:creator: Bowen Li, Jianfeng Lu

item.title: Endpoint gradient bounds for centered convex maximal operators and probability kernels
item.description: arXiv:2610.35760v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We establish the endpoint gradient estimate for centered homothetic maximal averages in every dimension $d\ge2$ over each fixed convex body with $C^{1,\theta}$ boundary, $0<\theta\le1$. In particular, the centered ball maximal operator satisfies the $W^{1,1}$ gradient bound in every dimension. Neither strict convexity nor a lower bound on the support gap is required. The geometric argument combines concentration in gradient values with nonhomogeneous calibrated rows and a summable radial correction. It extends the scalar refinement, direction-history construction and global assembly of the planar centered-disk proof of OpenAI. A separate transfer theorem gives sharp singular-derivative identities for bounded compact probability kernels once local BV output is known, and gradient continuity under an additional spatial-tail condition. Quantitative contact and translation estimates yield further profile and kernel examples. The estimates retain the fixed body's regularity data; the endpoint for arbitrary $C^1$ and nonsmooth convex bodies remains open here.
item.dc:creator: Zhouyu Long

item.title: Self-intersection local times of Volterra Gaussian bridges with large end-to-end distance
item.description: arXiv:2610.35769v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Self-intersection local times serve as the Hamiltonian in the Gibbs measure of continuous polymer models, for which the end-to-end distance is a key quantity. We study multiple self-intersection local times of Volterra Gaussian bridges, \emph{i.e.}, Volterra Gaussian processes conditioned on their final location $a$, as $\|a\|\to\infty$. For $d$-dimensional $(2,\zeta)$-locally nondeterministic processes with $\zeta\in(0,2/d)$, we prove that these local times exist in every $L^p$. Under two further conditions on the kernel, the $p$-th moment of the $m$-multiple self-intersection local time of the bridge is of exact order $\|a\|^{-\gamma}$ for every integer $p\geqslant1$, with $\gamma=p(m-1)(2-\zeta d)/(2-\zeta)$. In the plane, for kernels $k(t-s)$ with $k(0)\neq0$ and under strong local nondeterminism, we restrict the double self-intersection local time to $\{t_2-t_1\geqslant\|a\|^{-\alpha}\}$, $\alpha>0$, and establish a phase transition: its expectation decays like $\exp(-c\|a\|^{2-\alpha})$, converges to an explicit positive limit, or grows logarithmically, for $\alpha<2$, $\alpha=2$ and $\alpha>2$ respectively.
item.dc:creator: Olga Izyumtseva, Wasiur R. KhudaBukhsh

item.title: A solution to Haagerup's problem: Normality of weights is commutatively determined
item.description: arXiv:2610.35774v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove that a weight on a C$^*$-algebra is lower semi-continuous if it is lower semi-continuous on commutative C$^*$-subalgebras. This can be used to prove a von Neumann algebraic counterpart that a weight on a von Neumann algebra is normal if it is normal on commutative von Neumann subalgebras. This provides an affirmative solution to Haagerup's second problem (Problem 1.11) on normal weights posed in 1975.
item.dc:creator: David P. Blecher, Ikhan Choi

item.title: The $\varepsilon$-smoothed Entanglement of Formation and its relation to the Moreau-Yosida approximation
item.description: arXiv:2610.35797v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We describe a family of convex continuous functions $E_{F,\varepsilon}$, $\varepsilon\in(0,1]$, on the set of states of a bipartite quantum system (consisting of finite-dimensional or infinite-dimensional subsystems) obtained by applying the Mora-Piani-Briegel construction of $\varepsilon$-measure (proposed in [Phys. Rev. A 109, 052413]) to the Entanglement of Formation (EoF) with the use of the trace norm distance in the role of basic metric. These functions are non-increasing in $\varepsilon$ and converge pointwise to the EoF as $\varepsilon\to0^+$. We conducted a detailed analysis of properties of the functions $E_{F,\varepsilon}$, using (among others) the relationship between the family $\{E_{F,\varepsilon}\}_{\varepsilon\in[0,1]}$ and the family $\{E^\lambda_F(\rho)\}_{\lambda>0}$ of Moreau-Yosida approximations of the EoF explored in [arXiv:2609.30246]. We obtain a variational expression for the functions $E_{F,\varepsilon}$ (which for $\varepsilon=0$ turns into the standard variational expression for the EoF). We also describe the weak subadditivity property of the functions $E_{F,\varepsilon}$ and analyse their continuity properties. The semicontinuity bounds for the EoF (presented in [Lob.J.Math., 46, 2632-2658],[arXiv:2404.07978]) allow us to obtain easily computable upper bounds on the rate of uniform convergence of the function $E_{F,\varepsilon}$ to the EoF as $\varepsilon\to0^+$ on the sets of states with bounded rank/energy of one of the marginal states. Applicability of the obtained results to other entanglement measures, in particular, to the relative entropy of entanglement, is discussed. As an auxiliary result, it is shown that for any state of an infinite-dimensional bipartite quantum system, there exists a nearest separable state w.r.t. the trace norm distance. The non-uniqueness of such a state is also shown.
item.dc:creator: M. E. Shirokov

item.title: Complete entropy contraction from conditional hyperboundedness
item.dc:creator: Li Gao, Lijun Wang

item.title: Morse theory methods for a class of quasi-linear elliptic systems of higher order
item.description: arXiv:1709.02337v5 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We develop the local Morse theory for a class of non-twice continuously differentiable functionals on Hilbert spaces, including a new generalization of the Gromoll-Meyer's splitting theorem and a weaker Marino-Prodi perturbation type result. They are applicable to a wide range of multiple integrals with quasi-linear elliptic Euler equations and systems of higher order.
item.arxiv:journal_reference: Calc. Var. Partial Differential Equations 58 (2019), no. 4, Paper No. 134
item.dc:creator: Guangcun Lu

item.title: On the non-hypercyclicity of normal operators, collections of their exponentials, and symmetric operators
item.description: arXiv:1908.01935v5 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We give a simple, straightforward proof of the non-hypercyclicity of an arbitrary normal operator $A$ (bounded or unbounded) in a complex Hilbert space as well as of the collection $\left\{e^{tA}\right\}_{t\ge 0}$ of its exponentials, which, under a certain condition on the spectrum of $A$, is the $C_0$-semigroup generated by it. We also establish non-hypercyclicity for symmetric operators.
item.dc:creator: Marat V. Markin, Edward S. Sichel

item.title: On metric space expansions
item.description: arXiv:1908.04916v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: When finding an original proof to a known result describing expansions on compact metric spaces as surjective isometries, we reveal that relaxing the condition of compactness to total boundedness preserves the isometry property and nearly that of surjectivity. While a counterexample is found showing that the converse to the above descriptions do not hold, we are able to characterize boundedness in terms of specific expansions we call anticontractions.
item.dc:creator: Marat V. Markin, Edward S. Sichel

item.title: Group-Frames for Banach Spaces
item.description: arXiv:2305.01499v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In the literature, frames generated by unitary representations of groups (known as group-frames) have been studied only for Hilbert spaces. We conduct the first study of frames for Banach spaces generated by isometrically invertible representations of discrete groups on Banach spaces. These frames are characterized using left-regular and right-regular representations, Gram matrices, and group matrices on classical sequence spaces. A sufficiently large collection of functional-vector pairs using the double commutant of the representation is identified to generate group-frames for Banach spaces. Subsequently, we study Schauder frames generated by time-frequency shift operators on finite-dimensional Banach spaces. We derive the Moyal formula, the fundamental identity of Gabor analysis, the Wexler-Raz criterion, and the Ron-Shen duality in functional form.
item.dc:creator: K. Mahesh Krishna

item.title: Geometric Properties of Variable Mixed Lebesgue-Sequence Spaces
item.description: arXiv:2401.03211v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We investigate the geometric properties of the variable mixed Lebesgue sequence space \(\ell^{q(\cdot)}(L^{p(\cdot)})\). Assuming that \(q_->1\), \(p_+<\infty\), and \(q(\cdot)\le p(\cdot)\) almost everywhere, we prove that both \(\ell^{q(\cdot)}(L^{p(\cdot)})\) and its dual space are strictly convex and smooth. Moreover, we establish that \(\ell^{q(\cdot)}(L^{p(\cdot)})\) is uniformly convex under these assumptions. We further show that the condition \(q_->1\) is sharp: when \(q_-=1\), the space fails to be uniformly convex, and its modular is not uniformly convex either. Finally, we apply these geometric results to the renormability of the associated variable-exponent Besov space \(B_{p(\cdot),q(\cdot)}^{\alpha(\cdot)}\).
item.dc:creator: Arash Ghorbanalizadeh, Reza Roohi Seraji

item.title: Mixed-norm Herz-type Besov spaces
item.description: arXiv:2406.14727v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper, we introduce mixed-norm Herz-type Besov spaces and establish their $\varphi$-transform characterization in the sense of Frazier and Jawerth. We also prove Sobolev embedding theorems for these spaces. The resulting embeddings extend and improve several known embedding results for mixed-norm Besov spaces.
item.dc:creator: Douadi Drihem

item.title: A Complex Geometric Approach to the Discrete Gabor Transform and Localization Operators on the Flat Torus
item.description: arXiv:2410.15170v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In a recent paper, the discrete Gabor transform was connected to a Gabor transform with a time frequency domain given by the flat torus. We show that the corresponding Bargmann-Fock spaces can be expressed as theta functions (or equivalently line bundles on Abelian varieties). We give applications of this viewpoint to frame results for the discrete Gabor transform. In particular, we get necessary conditions which hold in higher dimensions and can expand the known results in the one dimensional case, the primary tool being the theorem of the square. We also give an application to asymptotics of restriction operators which arises via the asymptotic behavior of Bergman kernels and Toeplitz operators for high tensor powers of line bundles and find that discrete time frequency restriction operators will exhibit "plunge" behaviors similar to those of time frequency restriction operators in other contexts.
item.dc:creator: Johannes Testorf

item.title: Fej\'er--Riesz factorization for positive noncommutative trigonometric polynomials
item.description: arXiv:2511.09267v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove a Fej\'er-Riesz type factorization for positive matrix-valued noncommutative trigonometric polynomials on $\mathscr{W}\times\mathfrak{Y}$, where $\mathscr{W}$ is either the free semigroup $\langle x \rangle_g$ or the free product group $\mathbb{Z}_2^{g}$, and $\mathfrak{Y}$ is a discrete group. More precisely, using the shortlex order, if $A$ has degree at most $w$ in the $\mathscr{W}$ variables and is uniformly strictly positive on all unitary representations of $\mathscr{W}\times\mathfrak{Y}$, then $A=B^{*}B$ with $B$ analytic and of $\mathscr{W}$-degree at most $w$; this degree bound is optimal, and strict positivity is essential. As an application, we obtain degree-bounded sums-of-squares certificates for Bell-type inequalities in $\mathbb{C}[\mathbb{Z}_2^{*g}\times \mathbb{Z}_2^{*h}]$ from quantum information theory. In the special case $\mathscr{W}=\mathbb{Z}^h$ we recover, in the matrix-valued setting, the classical commutative multivariable Fej\'er-Riesz factorization. For trivial $\mathfrak{Y}$ we obtain a ``perfect'' group-algebra Positivstellensatz on $\mathbb{Z}_2^{*g}$ that does not require strict positivity; this result is sharp, as demonstrated by counterexamples in $\mathbb{Z}_2*\mathbb{Z}_3$ and $\mathbb{Z}_3^{*2}$. To establish our main results two novel ingredients of independent interest are developed: (a) a positive-semidefinite Parrott theorem with entries given by functions on a group; and (b) solutions to positive semidefinite matrix completion problems for $\langle x \rangle_g$ or the free product group $\mathbb{Z}_2^{*g}$ indexed by words in $\mathscr{W}$ of length $\le w$.
item.dc:creator: Igor Klep, Jacob Levenson, Scott McCullough

item.title: Uniform decay of function norms
item.description: arXiv:2511.19000v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We introduce and study two new relations between function spaces over measure spaces of infinite measure, motivated by the question of establishing compactness. The first relation captures the uniform decay of function (quasi-)norms ``at infinity''. It appeared implicitly in the first author's recent work on the compactness of Sobolev embeddings of radially symmetric functions on $\mathbb{R}^n$. The second is a suitably localized version of the relation of almost-compact embeddings, which has been successfully used to study compactness in function spaces over measure spaces of finite measure, but becomes of no use in the case of infinite measure. Our framework is that of quasi-Banach function spaces, which need not be normable or rearrangement invariant. This level of generality leads us to introduce the notion of extremal fundamental functions associated with a (quasi-)Banach function space. We provide several concrete examples and establish an abstract compactness principle involving the new relations. Finally, we demonstrate a possible application of this principle to embeddings of inhomogeneous Sobolev spaces on $\mathbb{R}^n$.
item.arxiv:journal_reference: J. Geom. Anal. 36 (2026), no. 12, paper no. 396, 43 pp
item.dc:creator: Zden\v{e}k Mihula, Maximili\'an P\'andy

item.title: Dunford-Pettis Multilinear Operators and Their Weak Variant on Banach Spaces
item.description: arXiv:2603.09687v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper, we address broader concepts of Dunford-Pettis operators, presenting new classes and results that relate this class to others already well studied in the literature, as well as an approach outside the origin. We also investigate inclusion results and conditions for the coincidence of this class with previously studied classes and with new classes that arise throughout this work.
item.dc:creator: Joilson Ribeiro, Fabricio Santos

item.title: On $c_0$ quotients of nonseparable Bourgain-Pisier $\mathscr{L}_\infty$-spaces
item.description: arXiv:2604.11832v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Lopez-Abad extended the Bourgain-Pisier construction to Banach spaces of arbitrary density: every Banach space $X$ embeds isometrically into an $\mathcal{L}_\infty$-space $Y$ such that $Y/X$ has the Radon-Nikodym and Schur properties. We study $c_0$ quotients of these spaces. For every $X$ of uncountable density $\kappa$, we describe a realization of the construction that admits an explicit surjection $T: Y \to c_0$, given by coordinate functionals built along the construction, whose kernel is an $\mathcal{L}_\infty$-space of density $\kappa$. We also note that an $\mathcal{L}_\infty$-space with a non-Grothendieck quotient has a $c_0$ quotient, and that every Lopez-Abad space has an $\ell_2$ quotient; all of them have $c_0$ quotients if no infinite-dimensional Banach space is both Schur and Grothendieck, a question we leave open. In an appendix we characterize when the kernel of a quotient map from an $\mathcal{L}_\infty$-space onto $c_0$ is an $\mathcal{L}_\infty$-space, give a quotient map from $C[0,1]$ onto $c_0$ whose kernel is not, and show that every non-Grothendieck $\mathcal{L}_\infty$-space admits one whose kernel is. This version corrects errors in version 1.
item.dc:creator: Kartik Patri

item.title: Block-equivalent finite Gabor frames
item.description: arXiv:2605.16139v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study finite systems of vectors whose frame operator matrices are unitarily equivalent, via explicit and computationally efficient unitary transformations, to block-diagonal matrices. We call such systems block-equivalent. We show that a Gabor system $\mathcal{G}=\mathcal{G}(g,L\times K)\subset \mathbb C^N$ is block-equivalent when either the modulation set $L$ or the translation set $K$ is a subgroup of $\mathbb Z_N$. We also characterize situations in which the frame operator matrix becomes diagonal. Finally, we show that geometric conditions on subsets of $\mathbb Z_N$ force certain diagonals of the frame operator matrix of $\mathcal{G}$ to vanish, yielding additional sparsity and block structures.
item.dc:creator: Oleg Asipchuk, Laura De Carli, Luis Rodriguez

item.title: Spectral embedding through weak* limit of finite-dimensional approximations
item.description: arXiv:2605.30186v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The scope of this text is to study a process that induces another proof of the Spectral Embedding Theorem: that any densely defined symmetric operator can be extended by a multiplication operator through an embedding of the Hilbert space into an $L_2$ space. Furthermore, that process is meant to be used for specific operators, where natural spectral embeddings or equivalences may be found. That process has previously been considered in arXiv:2411.06281 and in arXiv:2511.18189, where it has been introduced through nonstandard techniques. Our contribution aims to be the reformulation of the theory through classical analysis arguments, without the use of nonstandard techniques nor ultraproducts.
item.dc:creator: Fabrice Nonez

item.title: $\pi$-Properties, Uniformly Convexity and Uniform Ball Coverings Properties
item.description: arXiv:2607.12538v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper, we prove a sufficient condition for the uniform ball-covering property of closed operator subspaces invariant under selected truncations. We use uniform convexity of the range space and near-contractive finite-rank projection approximations to obtain quantitative coverings with finite-rank centres whenever the truncated images are separable. A weak-star version gives the same covering parameters for quotients by arbitrary weak-star closed subspaces. In the completely bounded setting, the covering parameters are independent of the matrix level. In particular, the duals of all closed subspaces of $S_1(\ell_2)$ admit coverings with centre norm $2$ and radius $1+\varepsilon$, for $0<\varepsilon<1$, at every matrix level. Applications include operator-valued Schur multipliers and, for $1<p<\infty$, prescribed-support Fourier multipliers on countable amenable groups and finitely generated free groups. The Fourier coverings have finite-support centres in the given operator or completely bounded norms. An endpoint example shows failure of the ball-covering property at $p=1,\infty$.
item.dc:creator: Rui Liu, Jie Shen

item.title: Comparing positive Toeplitz operators on holomorphic and pluriharmonic Fock spaces
item.description: arXiv:2608.13550v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove sharp norm comparisons between positive Toeplitz operators associated with the same positive Borel measure, acting respectively on holomorphic functions and on sums of holomorphic and antiholomorphic functions, both equipped with the Gaussian-weighted $L^2$ norm. For every positive Borel measure $\mu$ on $\mathbb{C}^n$ and $0<p<\infty$, both operators are compact with summable $p$th powers of their singular values (i.e. Schatten) exactly when $z\mapsto\mu(B(z,r))$ belongs to $L^p(\mathbb{C}^n)$ for some fixed radius $r>0$. For other weights, this agreement can fail dramatically. We construct a weight $e^{-2\phi}$ and a finite positive measure $\mu$ on $\mathbb{C}$ for which the operator on holomorphic functions has the same singular values as with the Gaussian weight and the same measure $\mu$. These values have summable $p$th powers for every $p>0$, yet the quadratic form on sums of holomorphic and antiholomorphic functions is unbounded in weighted $L^2$. The example still satisfies $\Delta\phi=2$, as for the Gaussian choice $\phi(z)=|z|^2/2$.
item.dc:creator: Sam Looi

item.title: Exponential Growth of Mean Multiplicities in Length Spectra of Semi-Arithmetic Surfaces of Arbitrary Arithmetic Dimension
item.description: arXiv:2608.17604v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: For a semi-arithmetic Fuchsian group $\Gamma$ of arithmetic dimension $r$ with a generalized modular embedding, EGMM holds for $r\leq2$, and for $r\geq3$ under an explicit \emph{strong contraction condition}, via a multi-dimensional Schwarz-Pick bound and a geometry-of-numbers estimate. A covering construction turns every known example into an infinite explicit family with the same exponent via principal congruence towers. We add new $r\leq2$ examples (genus-$3$/$4$ Prym eigenform loci, a different commensurability class from the known triangle groups and McMullen genus-two family) and attempt a direct flat-geometric bound on the contraction constant $\delta$ for the latter via its Lyapunov exponents ($\delta=2/3$ on ergodic average, by Bainbridge exact computation), explaining why an average bound does not yet certify the pointwise one \eqref{eqstrong-contraction} needs.
item.dc:creator: A. Zuevsky

item.title: Minimum attaining operators on reducing subspaces: Spectral structure and density
item.description: arXiv:2608.19286v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this article, we introduce and study the class $\mathcal{M}_r(H)$ of minimum attaining operators on a separable Hilbert space $H$ whose restrictions to every nonzero reducing subspace are minimum attaining. This class lies between the classes of absolutely minimum attaining operators and minimum attaining operators. We establish a spectral characterization of positive operators in $\mathcal{M}_r(H)$: a positive operator $T$ belongs to $\mathcal{M}_r(H)$ if and only if $T=\sum_{\lambda\in\Lambda}\lambda P_\lambda$, where $\Lambda\subseteq[0,\|T\|]$ is a countable well-ordered set, $(P_\lambda)_{\lambda\in\Lambda}$ is a family of mutually orthogonal nonzero projections, and $\sum_{\lambda\in\Lambda}P_\lambda=I$ in the strong operator topology. We also establish a connection between $\mathcal{M}_r(H)$ and the class of operators attaining their norm on every nonzero reducing subspace. Further, we obtain stability results under suitable finite-rank and compact perturbations, and prove that $\mathcal{M}_r(H)$ is norm dense in $\mathcal{B}(H)$.
