We also establish the norm density of operators in this class having a nontrivial invariant half-space. Finally, we characterize normal operators in $\mathcal{M}_r(H)$, obtain a corresponding characterization for multiplication operators on $L^2(\mathbb{T})$, and characterize the condition $\mathcal{R}_T=\mathcal{R}_{|T|}$ in terms of the von Neumann algebra generated by $|T|$, showing that this condition forces $T$ to be normal.
item.dc:creator: Nag Puspendu, Golla Ramesh

item.title: Critical Schatten exponents for the Berger-Coburn endpoint problem
item.description: arXiv:2609.11853v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Berger and Coburn showed that boundedness of a Toeplitz operator $T_g$ on the Fock space controls the heat transform $g^{(t)}$ for $1/4<t<1$, and conjectured that $T_g$ is bounded if and only if $g^{(1/4)}$ is bounded. Looi recently disproved the forward implication by constructing a bounded $T_g$ with unbounded $g^{(1/4)}$. We prove that the reverse implication also fails, even for a real-valued admissible symbol $g$ with $g^{(1/4)}\in C_0(\mathbb{C}^n)$, and that the forward implication fails even when $T_g\in S_p$ for every finite $p>1$. Our counterexamples come from Baire category and closed graph arguments, which yield no explicit symbols. Despite this two-sided failure, the forward implication has a sharp Schatten-class form: $\|g^{(1/4)}\|_\infty\le 2^n\|T_g\|_{S_1}$ for every admissible symbol $g$ with $T_g$ trace class. We show that the constant $2^n$ is optimal and that the same estimate holds with $S_p$ in place of $S_1$ for $T_g\in S_p$ when $0<p\le1$. For $p>1$, no corresponding uniform estimate holds, even for smooth compactly supported symbols. We also determine the optimal constants in the Berger--Coburn estimates for $1/4<t\le1$. Finally, for $1\le p<\infty$, we show that the equivalence $T_g\in S_p$ if and only if $g^{(1/4)}\in L^p$ holds exactly when $p=2$, answering a question of Bauer, Coburn, and Isralowitz.
item.dc:creator: Jani A. Virtanen

item.title: Fourier quasicrystals with positive integer masses are sections of Lee-Yang cycles
item.description: arXiv:2610.10652v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove that Fourier quasicrystal measures with positive integer masses are precisely the nonzero real sections of effective Lee-Yang cycles by matrices with positive maximal minors, with masses given by weighted local intersection degrees. For Delone support, the reduced support of the cycle can be chosen strict. For unit masses, the cycle can be chosen reduced, with local intersection degree one at every root. Every integer-mass FQ measure has support equal to the common complex zero set of finitely many real-valued trigonometric polynomials. These results answer Questions (1), (2), and (4) of Alon, Kummer, Kurasov, and Vinzant. We recover a finite-dimensional torus from the spectrum and prove that its canonical analytic set is algebraic. A support-height theorem for holonomic sequences provides a linear spectral bound, from which we reconstruct the complex branches and their integer coefficients using fiber moments. Singular sections carry their natural local intersection degrees; discarding these can destroy the Fourier quasicrystal property.
item.dc:creator: Dongsheng Wei

item.title: Geometric operators and the third problem of Halmos
item.description: arXiv:2610.12857v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In 1970, P. R. Halmos raised ten open problems on operator theory. The third problem of Halmos is the following: if an intransitive operator has an inverse, is its inverse also intransitive? This question is reduced to the case of conjugate bi-geometric operators in arXiv: 2610.11202. In the framework of conjugate bi-geometric operators, using tools from complex geometry, operator theory, and function theory, this paper gives an affirmative answer to the third problem of Halmos in the following cases: (a) bundle-preserving operator;(b) subexponential growth of operator norms. These two cases cover a large class of operators.
item.dc:creator: Kui Ji, Chunlan Jiang, Zhenyue Wang

item.title: Linear Preservers of Semipositivity and Minimal Semipositivity
item.description: arXiv:2610.27413v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We classify all real linear into preservers of semipositivity on $M_{m,n}(\mathbb{R})$, $m,n\ge2$, for arbitrary source and target pairs of proper cones, without assuming invertibility or a prescribed form. The classification consists of product maps $L(A)=XAY$ and degenerate maps $L(A)=\Psi(u^TA)$, subject to explicit necessary and sufficient cone conditions. For square minimal semipositivity with respect to the standard nonnegative orthant, preservation instead forces the operator to be invertible: for $n\ge2$, the linear into preservers are exactly the maps $L(A)=XAY$ and $L(A)=XA^TY$ with $X,Y$ invertible and $X^{-1},Y^{-1}\ge0$. We also classify all linear preservers of orthant semipositivity from $M_{2,2}(\mathbb{R})$ to $M_{1,3}(\mathbb{R})$ into three disjoint classes, two of which lie outside product form.
item.dc:creator: Yulong Tian, Jinli Xu

item.title: On cutoff via rigidity for high dimensional curved diffusions
item.description: arXiv:2412.15969v5 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We consider overdamped Langevin diffusions in Euclidean space, with curvature equal to the spectral gap. This includes the Ornstein--Uhlenbeck process as well as non-Gaussian and non-product extensions with convex interaction, such as the Dyson process from random matrix theory. We show that a cutoff phenomenon or abrupt convergence to equilibrium occurs in high dimension, at a critical time equal to the logarithm of the dimension divided by twice the spectral gap. This cutoff holds for Wasserstein distance, total variation, relative entropy, and Fisher information. A key observation is a relation to a spectral rigidity, linked to the presence of a Gaussian factor. A novelty is the extensive usage of functional inequalities, even for short-time regularization, and the reduction to Wasserstein. The proofs are short and conceptual. Since the product condition is satisfied, an Lp cutoff holds for all finite p. We moreover discuss a natural extension to Riemannian manifolds, a link with logarithmic gradient estimates in short-time for the heat kernel, and ask about stability by perturbation. Finally, beyond rigidity but still for diffusions, a discussion around the recent progress on the product condition for non-negatively curved diffusions leads us to introduce a new curvature product condition.
item.dc:creator: Djalil Chafa\"i, Max Fathi

item.title: On the cutoff phenomenon for fast diffusion and porous medium equations
item.description: arXiv:2503.11770v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The cutoff phenomenon, conceptualized at the origin for finite Markov chains, states that for a parametric family of evolution equations, started from a point, the distance towards a long time equilibrium may become more and more abrupt for certain choices of initial conditions, when the parameter tends to infinity. This threshold phenomenon can be seen as a critical competition between trend to equilibrium and worst initial condition. In this note, we investigate this phenomenon beyond stochastic processes, in the context of the analysis of nonlinear partial differential equations, by proving cutoff for the fast diffusion and porous medium Fokker-Planck equations on the Euclidean space, when the dimension tends to infinity. We formulate the phenomenon using quadratic Wasserstein distance, as well as using specific relative entropy and Fisher information. Our high dimensional asymptotic analysis uses the exact solvability of the model involving Barenblatt profiles. It includes the Ornstein-Uhlenbeck dynamics as a special linear case.
item.dc:creator: Djalil Chafa\"i, Max Fathi, Nikita Simonov

item.title: On shallow feedforward neural networks with inputs from a topological space
item.description: arXiv:2504.02321v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study feedforward neural networks with inputs from a topological space (TFNNs). We prove a universal approximation theorem for shallow TFNNs, which demonstrates their capacity to approximate any continuous function defined on this topological space. As an application, we obtain an approximative version of Kolmogorov's superposition theorem for compact metric spaces.
item.arxiv:journal_reference: V.E. Ismailov, Ann. Math. Artif. Intell. (2026)
item.dc:creator: Vugar Ismailov

item.title: Hyper-dual group inverse: existence, characterizations, and applications
item.description: arXiv:2504.05264v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Motivated by the recent work of Xiao and Zhong [AIMS Math. 9 (2024), 35125--35150: MR4840882], we propose a generalized inverse for a hyper-dual matrix called hyper-dual group generalized inverse (HDGGI). Firstly, we characterize the existence of the HDGGI of a hyper-dual matrix and we show that it is unique, whenever exists. The HDGGI is then used to solve a linear hyper-dual system. We discuss the minimal $P$-norm least-squares properties of hyper-dual group inverse. We also exploit some sufficient conditions under which the reverse and forward-order laws for a particular form of the HDGGI and hyper-dual Moore-Penrose generalized inverse (HDMPGI) hold. Using the definition of dual matrix of order $n$, we finally establish necessary and sufficient condition for the existence of the group inverse of a dual matrix of order $n$.
item.dc:creator: Tikesh Verma, Amit Kumar, Vaibhav Shekhar, Nestor Thome

item.title: Topological cones and positively polarizable hyperbolic norms
item.description: arXiv:2508.17052v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In the first part of this article, we study linear cones over totally ordered fields. We show that for each such cone there uniquely exists a universal vector space (called its spanned vector space) into which it embeds as a generating convex cone. Moreover, we investigate topologies on cones for which the natural cone operations are continuous, and study how these topologies carry over to the spanned vector space. In the second part, we deal with hyperbolic norms which satisfy a polarization identity and are defined on cones over the real numbers. We show that, under reasonable assumptions, such hyperbolic norms induce a Lorentzian inner product on the spanned vector space. Finally, we establish a link between completeness under the Wick rotation of a Lorentzian inner product and order-theoretic completeness.
item.dc:creator: Ethan Kharitonov, Argam Ohanyan

item.title: Hausdorff content $A_p$ weights: weighted maximal inequalities and fundamental structural properties
item.description: arXiv:2509.23839v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Let $\mathcal H_{\infty}^\delta$ denote the Hausdorff content of dimension $\delta\in(0,n]$ defined on subsets of $\mathbb R^n$. The principal problem, considered in this paper, is to characterize the non-negative function $w$ for which the weighted $L^p$ inequality with $p\in(1,\infty)$ and the weighted weak $L^1$ inequality on Hardy-Littlewood maximal operators associated with Hausdorff content hold true. To achieve this, we introduce a class of Hausdorff content $A_p$ weights, denoted as $\mathcal A_{p,\delta}$, and then show that, for any $p\in(1,\infty)$ and $\delta\in(0,n]$, the weighted $L^p$ maximal inequality holds true if and only if $w\in\mathcal A_{p,\delta}$, and the weighted weak $L^1$ maximal inequality holds true if and only if $w\in\mathcal A_{1,\delta}$ by proposing a novel approach. As the second objective, applying this approach, the seminal structural properties of classical Muckenhoupt $A_p$ weights, such as the reverse H\"older inequality [R. R. Coifman and C. Fefferman, Studia Math. 51 (1974), 241-250], the self-improving property [B. Muckenhoupt, Trans. Amer. Math. Soc. 165 (1972), 207-226], and Jones' factorization theorem [P. W. Jones, Ann. of Math. (2) 111 (1980), 511-530], are all established for $\mathcal A_{p,\delta}$. The main novelties of this paper lies in: (i) we discover $\mathcal A_{p,\delta}$ weights with rich structural properties, that increase strictly on dimension exponent and hence reduce to the classical $A_p$ class at the endpoint dimension, forming proper subsets of it for smaller dimension exponent; (ii) by proposing a novel approach, this work naturally extends the classical theory beyond measure-theoretic frameworks, while also provides novel insights even when reduced to the classical $A_p$ weight case.
item.dc:creator: Long Huang, Yangzhi Zhang, Ciqiang Zhuo

item.title: Higher-order Persistence Diagrams
item.description: arXiv:2605.09866v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Persistent homology tracks when topological features appear and disappear across filtered data and represents the lifetime of each feature by a persistence interval. In multiple instance learning, when the instances in a bag use filtrations over the same ordered parameter space, we can compare relationships between persistence intervals across instances. No existing method is designed to aggregate collections of persistence diagrams in multiple instance learning into a single persistence diagram of implications between intervals. We introduce higher-order persistence diagrams to represent relationships between persistence intervals and recursively construct each higher-order persistence interval from a pair of lower-order persistence intervals. We then aggregate these relationships across the persistence diagrams in a bag. Explicit construction of this aggregate is computationally expensive, so we introduce harmonic aggregation to compute coordinates of the aggregate from the lower-order persistence diagrams without explicitly constructing it. Computing a harmonic aggregation coordinate has lower asymptotic computational complexity than explicitly constructing the aggregate. We evaluate harmonic aggregation against persistence landscapes, persistence images, and PersLay on random network model and real-world graph-classification benchmarks, and find that harmonic aggregation has the highest accuracy on the random network model benchmark and on most real-world data benchmarks. Source code is available at https://github.com/cfanning8/higher-order-PDs.
item.dc:creator: Charles Fanning, Mehmet Aktas

item.title: A Banach space that distinguishes two maximal operators
item.description: arXiv:2605.17663v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Maz'ya and Shaposhnikova introduced a non-classical maximal operator $M^\diamond$ as the maximal convolution with the vector-valued signum kernel truncated to centered balls. We construct a translation-invariant Banach space of locally integrable functions on which $M^\diamond$ is bounded, but the sharp maximal operator $M^\sharp$ is not. This answers one of Maz'ya's questions from a collection of 75 open problems in analysis.
item.dc:creator: Vjekoslav Kova\v{c}

item.title: Ubiquity in the setting of forward-reverse Brascamp-Lieb inequalities
item.description: arXiv:2606.26500v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The ubiquity of geometric Brascamp-Lieb data, which refers to a certain density property of geometric data within the set of all feasible Brascamp-Lieb data, has recently been studied. Motivated in part by a question of Bennett-Tao concerning a possible connection or analogue of the adjoint Brascamp-Lieb inequality to the forward-reverse Brascamp-Lieb inequality, we establish ubiquity in the forward-reverse setting. Our proof takes an analytic approach and, to overcome the difficulties arising in extending ubiquity to the forward-reverse setting, makes use of tools from the calculus of variations such as Danskin's theorem and Ekeland's variational principle.
item.dc:creator: Mirei Watanabe

item.title: A point-free theory of quantitative homogenization
item.description: arXiv:2608.05077v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We introduce a purely operator-theoretic framework for quantitative homogenization that bypasses the traditional reliance on large-scale spatial regularity and probabilistic assumptions. Inspired by Tartar's vision of a point-free theory, we derive explicit norm resolvent estimates using only the algebraic structure of multiscale operators and the abstract geometry of Hilbert spaces. In this framework, the effective macroscopic dynamics and the abstract corrector emerge naturally from an orthogonal decomposition of the state space, governed algebraically by a Schur complement. To quantify the convergence rate, we introduce a frequency-splitting technique and a flux corrector obtained by inverting the microscopic derivative on the residual field; this controls the error for regular macroscopic data in terms of explicit, $\varepsilon$-independent operator norms. This abstract perspective places on one footing stationary, non-stationary, periodic, quasi-periodic, and stochastic homogenization. We demonstrate that the physical distinctions between these media---and their respective convergence rates---are captured by the behavior of the spectral measure of the microscopic derivative operator, evaluated on the residual field, near zero frequency; in the periodic case the rate $O(\varepsilon)$ is proved, while in the stochastic case the rates are conditional on a density-of-states hypothesis. Furthermore, our results apply for multiscale systems that do not uphold subadditivity of energy quantities or do not have a well-defined Brillouin zone.
item.dc:creator: Thuyen Dang, Yuliya Gorb, Silvia Jim\'enez Bola\~nos

item.title: A Near-Optimal Lower Bound for $\ell_p$-Subspace Embeddings, $1\leq p<2$
item.description: arXiv:2608.14201v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: For $d \geq 2$, $p \geq 1$ and $\epsilon > 0$, let $N_p(d,\epsilon)$ be the smallest integer $N$ such that for every integer $n$ and every $A\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times d}$, there exists a matrix $\Phi\in\mathbb{R}^{N\times n}$ satisfying $(1-\epsilon)\lVert Ax\rVert_p\leq \lVert\Phi A x\rVert_p\leq (1+\epsilon)\lVert Ax\rVert_p$ for all $x\in\mathbb{R}^d$. For every constant $p\geq 1$ with $p\not\in 2\mathbb{Z}$, when $d\gtrsim_p \log(1/\epsilon)$, the bound \[ N_p(d,\epsilon) \gtrsim_{p} \frac{d}{\epsilon^2 \operatorname{polylog}(d/\epsilon)} \] is established. This improves the previous lower bound $\Omega(1/(\epsilon^2\operatorname{polylog}(1/\epsilon)))$ due to Li et al. (SICOMP 2021) and is optimal up to logarithmic factors for $1\leq p<2$. The central technical idea originated from ChatGPT 6 Pro.

item.title: Wehrl-type entropy problem for compact connected semisimple Lie groups
item.description: arXiv:2609.18919v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Let $G$ be a compact connected semisimple Lie group, and let $\pi:G\to U(V_\lambda)$ be a finite-dimensional irreducible unitary representation associated with the highest weight $\lambda$. We prove that coherent projectors are the unique minimizers of the Wehrl entropy over all density matrices on $V_\lambda$. Similar extremal properties hold for power functions in place of the entropy function. The proof uses a second variation at the extremizer by perturbation in directions associated with Killing fields, similar to the strategy of Frank and Lieb used in \cite{FrankLieb}. Then the problem reduces to the uncertainty principle characterizing coherent states. This solves the Wehrl-type entropy problem for arbitrary compact connected semisimple Lie groups.

item.title: Normalised Hamiltonian Elliptic Systems: a Gagliardo-Nirenberg inequality for bilinear mass
item.description: arXiv:2610.08774v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study Hamiltonian elliptic systems with prescribed bilinear mass $\int_{\mathbb{R}^N}uv=a>0$. We establish a Gagliardo--Nirenberg inequality in the crossed gradient pairing and bilinear mass, on scaling-invariant component-bounded classes. It identifies the critical curve $1/p+1/q=N/(N+2)$ and the restricted energy trichotomy. For power nonlinearities, we establish uniqueness up to common translations and nondegeneracy of positive profiles throughout the Sobolev-subcritical hyperbola. Exact scaling then classifies positive normalised solutions and identifies the unique critical mass. In dimension two, we develop a bilinear exponential Gagliardo--Nirenberg estimate with a sharp gradient threshold and a truncated scalar refinement with the optimal quartic leading coefficient. Adapting variational ideas from [Cassani-Tarsi, Calc.Var.PDE (2015)] we combine a mass-normalising quotient, reduction over the full negative fibres and compactness below the concentration threshold to obtain least-energy positive radial solutions for pure exponential nonlinearities at every prescribed mass below the cubic limiting mass. Local perturbative branches and a small-frequency exponential branch yield explicit mass-response formulas.

item.title: Sharp noncommutative Hilbert and Riesz inequalities: classification and spectral corrections
item.description: arXiv:2610.10158v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: For every $1<p<\infty$, with $p^*=\max\{p,p/(p-1)\}$, we determine the sharp Hilbert norm $C_p=\cot(\pi/(2p^*))$ on $L^p(\mathbb{R};\mathcal{S}_p)$ and the sharp uniform bound $D_p=\csc(\pi/p)$ for retained and strict Riesz projections of maximal subdiagonal algebras in finite tracial von Neumann algebras. The Hilbert value is also the common Fourier--Schur completely bounded norm. For finite matrices, a nonnegative logarithmic determinant defect connects Hein\"avaara's tracial joint spectral measure to eigenvalues. The resulting transfer identity classifies finite signed real ridge inequalities on nilpotents and identifies their least additive eigenvalue corrections. A dual theorem characterizes weak-* limits of weighted angular measures of finite nilpotents. In general finite tracial algebras, separate positive-kernel and sharp determinant-covariance comparisons yield the Riesz bounds. Consequences include the sharp Volterra constant, Riesz--Titchmarsh and shifted-transform formulas, joint real-pencil norms, and exact triangular and operator-valued Fourier Riesz norms.
